requirement_or_question: Archives packed from the same logical tree require different incompatible feature bits depending on the packing host: default Windows capture always sets FEATURE_PLATFORM_SECURITY_METADATA_V1 (0x10000) for AUX-only security descriptors, while Linux ext4 capture without ACLs does not. The baseline test cross_file_compression::small_cohort_stays_independent_and_v2_v3_remain_readable hard-codes the Windows outcome and fails on Linux.
implementation_evidence: Reproduced by research/harness/repro_cross_file_linux.sh at 9e44608 on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (left 0x8001, right 0x18001); passes on the Windows 11 host.
research_needed: Measure, across platforms and default capture policies, which feature bits real archives require; assess reader fail-closed impact for minimal/independent readers; fix test portability.
decision_needed: Should AUX-only platform metadata make an archive unreadable to readers lacking that feature (incompatible bit), or be gated by per-record criticality or a compatible tier?

question: Which feature-tier mechanism should gate AUX-only platform metadata (e.g. platform-security-metadata-v1) so that Windows-created archives are not unreadable to readers lacking that metadata support, without violating fail-closed semantics for critical facts?
archetypal_objective: Entrybound must fail closed on unknown critical semantics while keeping archives independently implementable and portable; making non-identity auxiliary metadata a hard readability gate on every Windows-created archive raises minimal-reader cost and adoption friction without protecting logical content.

candidate_set.description: Keep platform security metadata as an incompatible feature bit whenever captured (current behavior).
Move AUX-only platform metadata to a compatible/read-only feature tier: readers may extract logical content while reporting unsupported AUX metadata through FidelityReport.
Keep the feature declared but mark AUX platform metadata records non-critical so unknown-record handling reports rather than refuses.
Do not capture Windows security descriptors by default; require explicit caller policy, so default archives do not require the feature.
Separate portable and platform-preservation identity/capture profiles, with only the latter requiring the feature.

required_evidence: Cross-platform packing experiment recording required feature bits for default capture on Windows NTFS, Linux ext4/XFS/btrfs, and (blocked) macOS APFS
Minimal/independent reader implementation cost with and without platform-security-metadata support
Analysis of fail-closed semantics for AUX-only records against spec §20.1-§20.2 and I12

requirement_or_question: Packing the same logical tree on Windows (NTFS) and Linux (ext4) yields different LAI because Windows capture records core.executable=false where the execute bit is unobservable, while Linux records true for mode 0755 files; PCR is identical across hosts.
implementation_evidence: EXP-DET-SMOKE balanced-indexed inspect diff: core_executable differs in 8/52 entries (Windows false, Linux true); LAI differs in 8/8 profile x layout cells; PCR equal in 8/8.
research_needed: Enumerate every LAI-participating field whose value is unobservable on some capture platform; measure LAI stability across Windows/Linux (and macOS when unblocked) for real corpus trees; evaluate tri-state (unknown) encodings and their wire/identity cost.
decision_needed: How should LAI represent semantics the capturing platform cannot observe (e.g. executable state on NTFS)?

question: How should identity-participating semantics that a capture platform cannot observe (e.g. POSIX executable state on NTFS) be represented so that LAI is canonical across packing hosts without inventing facts?
archetypal_objective: LAI is meant to be a canonical, host-independent identity of logical content; recording an unobservable fact as a definite value either fabricates semantics or makes identity depend on the packing OS.

candidate_set.description: Record executable=false when unobservable (current Windows behavior).
Add an explicit unknown state for executable (and other unobservable LAI facts) that participates in LAI distinctly.
Require an explicit caller policy on platforms where the fact is unobservable (e.g. infer from extension, a git index, or a manifest), recorded in FidelityReport.
Move executable state out of LAI into AUX so that LAI covers only facts observable on every platform.
Capture executable state from a portable source of truth (e.g. git tree modes) when packing checkouts.

required_evidence: Cross-host LAI stability experiment over real corpus trees (Windows NTFS vs Linux ext4/XFS/btrfs)
Inventory of LAI-participating fields and their observability per platform
Wire and identity cost of a tri-state encoding
Extraction semantics for unknown executable state

requirement_or_question: AUX differs across packing hosts for identical timestamps because the recorded timestamp precision reflects the capturing filesystem (Hectonanosecond on NTFS vs Nanosecond on ext4).
implementation_evidence: EXP-DET-SMOKE balanced-indexed inspect diff: core_mtime precision differs in 52/52 entries with equal seconds/nanoseconds.
research_needed: Determine whether precision is a restorability promise or incidental; measure AUX stability across hosts and filesystems.
decision_needed: Should recorded timestamp precision be canonicalized, and should it participate in AUX?

question: Should timestamp precision recorded from the capturing filesystem be canonicalized (or excluded) so identical instants yield identical AUX across hosts?
archetypal_objective: Auxiliary identity should reflect preserved metadata, not incidental properties of the capture host, while still truthfully declaring restorability limits.

candidate_set.description: Record the capturing filesystem's precision in AUX (current).
Canonicalize the recorded precision to the value's actual resolution (e.g. trailing-zero normalization) and report host limits in FidelityReport.
Keep precision as a non-identity capture observation outside AUX.

required_evidence: AUX stability experiment across NTFS, ext4, XFS, btrfs captures of identical instants
